title: James Wilkinson ('Agent 13') ↔ Spanish governors of Louisiana: cipher letters in two dictionary-and-table codes, most pages unread
correspondents: James Wilkinson → Spanish governors of Louisiana / agents of the Spanish Crown (Miró, Carondelet, Gayoso; not itemised in the source), and replies
date: c. 1789-1806 (letters undated in the released transcriptions)
shelfmark: Library of Congress, Manuscript Division, reproductions of the Archivo General de Indias, Papeles procedentes de Cuba, legajo 2374 (LoC page numbers 1524-1652, 2874-3072; 'File 1', 'File A', 'File B'); originals AGI Cuba leg. 2374
folio_note: Per the Chu/Valenti/Knight project inventory (github c2huc2hu/wilkinson data.txt): about 73 pp of ciphertext without decipherment and 28 pp with interlinear decipherment. Two systems: the '1078' code (table of ~1,240 numbered words with caret, plus page.row dictionary references with one or two bars for the column; dictionary ~780 pp x 2 cols x 29 rows) and a different '1096' system. Unsolved pages: LoC 1524, 1576-1583, 1598-1600, 1630-1631, 1642-1643, 2874, 2888-2890, 2895-2898, 2907-2909, 2930, 2943-2946, 2951-2953, 2962-2965, 2972, 3044-3047; decipherments for 1614-1624 and 1635-1637 exist (LoC 2975-2989, 3014-3018) but the project did not have the scans.
status: Partly read. Chu, Valenti and Knight (EMNLP Findings 2020, arXiv 2010.04746) recovered 75.1% of cipher-word tokens on a held-out 500-token excerpt (LoC 3044-3045) by a known-plaintext wordbank from the deciphered pages plus a neural LM; the dictionary itself was never identified and the 1096 system was not attacked. Not in the repo (known.py: no hits for 2374, Papeles de Cuba, Wilkinson cipher). Not on DECODE as far as checked.
why: Wilkinson's paid espionage for Spain while commanding the US Army is a major early-republic affair; the unread letters would document what he sold and when, including the Burr period.
language: English (some French words in the plaintext)

title: Robert Bunch, British consul at Charleston: four unsolved letter-group cryptograms (Schmeh/Beveridge challenge)
correspondents: Robert Bunch → unknown (British consular / Foreign Office channel)
shelfmark: Holding not named in print: notes found by Christopher Dickey while writing 'Our Man in Charleston' (2015); scans passed to Colin Beveridge
folio_note: Five notes; #1 a simple substitution ('stop the fools', solved); #2 c. 29 four-letter groups + 10 on reverse, #3 24 groups, #4 37 groups, #5 image only
status: Posted unsolved by Schmeh 1 June 2018; #1 read by Beveridge, #2-#5 open: Playfair, double Playfair, periodic polyalphabetic and codebook hypotheses all failed (Lasry's Playfair solver included). No later solution found 27 Oct 2026.
why: The cipher traffic of Britain's consul-agent in the Confederacy, who reported on secession and the slave trade to Lord Russell, could show what he sent outside the official despatches.

status: Transcription phase done; the planned decipherment phase with the Eckert cipher books is not reported as completed (checked 27 Oct 2026). Overlaps the Cryptoole draft row 'The "Decoding the Civil War" Project' (research/cryptoole/candidates.json, from cryptiana), which has no shelfmark; this row adds the holding. Milroy telegrams (same system) are already solved here. 27 Oct 2026 (WAINUT, PR #112; targets/eckert1862/, in progress): deciphering with the Eckert cipher books under way.
why: Thousands of War Department cipher telegrams, keys in the same collection: a large, keyed, mechanical reading task rather than a cryptanalytic one.

title: John J. Appleton → John Quincy Adams, Cadiz, despatch with an 18-group coded passage on the Spanish liberal government's secret English loan, printed 'no decodification'
correspondents: John James Appleton (US chargé d'affaires ad interim at Madrid, with the Cortes at Cadiz) → John Quincy Adams, Secretary of State
shelfmark: NARA RG 59, Despatches from US Ministers to Spain, vol. 22 (20 May 1822-30 Dec 1823) = microfilm M31 reel 24, catalog naId 188609418
folio_note: 18 code groups in the body (Manning prints them: 1088 648 1576 794 1384 1453 347 1372 500 192 668 1384 169 1244 1501 1110 1426 1290; several OCR-uncertain); frame not located Frame located 27 Oct 2026 (NARA bulk scan, research/nara_triage_a/): M31 reel 24, frame 0134.
status: Manning, Diplomatic Correspondence ... Independence of the Latin-American Nations (1925) vol. 3, doc. 1124, p. 2041, prints the groups with '[no decodification]'. The groups fit the code rebuilt in targets/jqa (the = 1385, of = 1576, that = 1384, and = 668; the London/St Petersburg code): with targets/jqa/code_table.tsv 16 of 18 groups take a value ('... of [794] that ... was [192] and that he had a part in England'). Not in the repo (known.py: Appleton no hits).
why: The Spanish constitutional government's secret plan to raise money in England in the last weeks of the Cortes at Cadiz (1823), told to the US chargé by the finance minister Yandiola; directly readable with a key this repository already holds.
source: NARA RG 59 diplomatic despatches (via Manning 1925) sweep
